editorial:
Imagine spending your whole life feeling invisible, only to suddenly have a group of cool, young artists tell you that you are a god. That is exactly what happens to Ed Saxberger. He is just a regular guy working at the post office who wrote some poems years ago that nobody liked. Then, a girl named Gloria and her group of artsy friends show up and treat him like a superstar. You will feel for Ed as he gets swept up in the excitement, but you will also start to wonder if these people actually like his work or if they are just playing a prank on him. The vibe is a mix of awkwardness and tension that keeps you guessing.

What really makes this work is the acting, especially the way the tension builds between Ed and Gloria. The pacing is steady, though some parts feel a bit slow until the big reveal. If you like stories about fame and lying, you will love this. You should definitely stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the gritty 70s details, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. It is a great pick if you want something that makes you think about what is real and what is fake.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, you find out that Gloria and her friends were actually running a cruel social experiment. They never liked the poetry; they just wanted to see how far they could push a lonely man's ego. Ed discovers the truth when he overhears them laughing about him. Instead of fighting back, he realizes he prefers the lie to his boring life, but he leaves the group alone and returns to his post office job, finally at peace with being unknown.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about social manipulation and lonely people.
